transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I guess what finally made me come in is this whole historical society fundraiser I got myself tangled up in. I took it on like I was going to run the entire thing myself, and at the time it felt completely reasonable, like I could just organize everything if people would let me.

I started designing quilts for it, calling volunteers, making schedules, setting up who would do what, and I was promising people deadlines that… looking back, I don’t think I could possibly have met. But in the moment I was just going and going with it, like every idea needed to be acted on right away. It got to where I realized I’d overcommitted myself badly, and I think that’s what scared me enough to come talk to someone.

After you realized you had overcommitted yourself with the fundraiser, did you feel down or lose interest in things for a period of time, or did your mood stay more consistently elevated or pressured?

It didn’t really stay up, no. After that sort of rush of trying to manage everything, I just… kind of went flat. The thing I notice most is that I used to love going out and checking my garden, seeing what was coming up, fussing over the plants, and I’d spend ages looking through seed catalogs like it was a treat.

And my quilts too — I usually enjoy planning my own entries, picking fabrics, laying them out, imagining how it’ll all come together. Lately I just look at the fabric, or the seed catalogs, and there’s not much there. I don’t feel excited or interested the way I normally would. It’s like I know those things are supposed to matter to me, and they usually do, but right now I’m just staring at them and feeling… not much at all.
Have there been times when your mood was noticeably more elevated, irritable, or energized in a way that was different from how you usually feel, even outside of projects like the fundraiser?

Yes… yes, there have been times like that. It’s not just the fundraiser, though that’s the one that made it obvious. Sometimes I’ll get into this state where at first I feel almost… glowing, I guess is the word. Like my mind is lit up and every idea I have seems not just good, but wonderful, like of course it should be done and of course I’m the one who can make it happen.

And when I’m in it, it doesn’t feel strange to me at the time. It feels like I’m finally clear, finally moving, finally seeing what everyone else is missing. But then if someone questions me — even gently, like “Are you sure?” or “Maybe that’s too much” — I can get really snappish. I hate admitting that, because I don’t think of myself as a nasty person, but I’ll act like they’re standing in my way or trying to hold me back. I’ll hear myself being sharp and still feel, in that moment, like they’re the problem for not keeping up.

So yes, elevated, energized… and irritable too, especially if anyone pushes back.

Have you ever experienced one of those elevated or energized moods when things in your life were actually going pretty well — not in response to a specific project or stressor, just kind of on their own?

Yes… I think so. I mean, that’s part of what makes it confusing to me, because it hasn’t always been after something bad happened or because I was under pressure. Sometimes things are just ordinary, or even going pretty smoothly, and then I’ll get this feeling like I’m suddenly brighter inside, if that makes sense.

At first it feels wonderful. I’ll feel almost glowing, like every idea I have is a good one — not just good, but important, like it has to be acted on. And I can be so sure of myself in those moments. It’s hard to explain because at the time it doesn’t feel like a problem. It feels like I’m finally seeing clearly.

But then if someone questions me, even in a normal way, I can turn snappish. I’ll act like they’re blocking me or standing in my way, when maybe they’re just trying to be reasonable. I don’t like that part of it. Looking back, I can see it’s different from how I usually am.
How long do these elevated or energized moods usually last? Do they tend to come and go quickly, or do they last for several days or even longer?

They definitely don’t just come and go in an afternoon, at least not the big ones. I mean, I might have little bursts where I’m wound up for a day or two, but the one with the historical society project — the really overdriven stretch — that went on for about five months.

It’s strange saying that out loud, because while it was happening it didn’t feel like “five months of something being wrong.” It felt like I was just working hard and being productive and, you know, carrying the whole thing because it needed carrying. But looking back, it was months of being in that pushed, driven state before everything finally fell apart. Five months, roughly.

latest_inference.note: The patient has reported a history of elevated, energized, and irritable mood states that occur independently of stressors and last for extended periods (e.g., five months), meeting criteria for hypomanic or manic episodes. These episodes are not solely related to the fundraiser but occur in the context of the patient's usual pattern. The presence of both depressive and hypomanic episodes supports the diagnosis of bipolar II disorder (F31.81).
